title: ESP-NOW multi-node networks: star topology and reliable delivery

spans.text: ESP-NOW carries short messages between ESP devices without joining an IP network or router. A star is a simple multi-node starting point: a coordinator registers each node's MAC as a peer, sends telemetry in turn, or collects acknowledgements. All nodes must use the same Wi-Fi channel. The example encodes fields into seven bytes in big-endian order to avoid compiler padding; receivers must decode the same format.

This small design sends telemetry from one coordinator to two peers. ESP-NOW does not provide mesh routing by itself: as nodes grow, design channel planning, target peer limits, acknowledgements/retries, sequence numbers, duplicate suppression, and gateway forwarding explicitly. Test same-channel peers, a wrong-channel peer, a lost ACK, and a duplicate sequence number.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: The MAC addresses and unencrypted peer settings are demonstration values. A real device needs verified peer addresses, PMK/LMK encryption keys, and input validation. A successful `esp_now_send()` does not prove that the receiver processed the packet; the receiver must implement application ACKs, sequence numbers, and timeout/retry handling. ESP-NOW is not automatic mesh routing; node/peer limits, callback APIs, and channel behavior depend on chip and core version.
